questions.q: The radius of a circle is increasing at $3$ cm/s. When the radius is $10$ cm, the area is increasing at:
questions.solution:
$A = \pi r^{2}$, so $\dfrac{dA}{dt} = 2\pi r \dfrac{dr}{dt}$.

$= 2\pi (10)(3) = \mathbf{60\pi}$ cm$^{2}$/s.

Notice the area grows faster the bigger the circle already is: new area is added around the **rim**, and a longer rim takes more of it.

questions.q: A differentiable function $f$ is strictly increasing on an interval if, throughout that interval:
questions.solution:
The derivative is the slope. A positive slope everywhere means the graph climbs everywhere — that is exactly strictly increasing.

$f''(x) > 0$ is a different statement: it says the climb is getting steeper (the curve bends upwards), which can happen while the function is still falling.

questions.q: The slope of the tangent to the curve $y = x^{3} - 3x$ at $x = 2$ is:
questions.solution:
$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 3x^{2} - 3$.

At $x = 2$: $3(4) - 3 = \mathbf{9}$.

The derivative is a speedometer for the curve — read it at the moment you care about.

questions.q: The maximum value of $\sin x + \cos x$ is:
questions.solution:
Write it as a single wave: $\sin x + \cos x = \sqrt{2}\,\sin\left(x + \tfrac{\pi}{4}\right)$.

A sine never exceeds $1$, so the maximum is $\mathbf{\sqrt{2}}$, reached at $x = \tfrac{\pi}{4}$.

Two waves of equal height a quarter-turn apart add up to one wave, taller by a factor of $\sqrt{2}$ — never to twice the height, because they never peak together.

questions.q: If $f'(c) = 0$ and $f''(c) > 0$, then at $x = c$ the function $f$ has:
questions.solution:
$f'(c) = 0$ says the tangent is flat; $f''(c) > 0$ says the curve is bending upwards there — a valley floor.

So $f$ has a **local minimum** at $c$. (Bending downwards, $f''(c) < 0$, would make it a peak.)

questions.q: The side of a square is increasing at $4$ cm/s. Find the rate (in cm$^{2}$/s) at which its area increases when the side is $8$ cm.
questions.solution:
$A = x^{2}$, so $\dfrac{dA}{dt} = 2x\dfrac{dx}{dt} = 2(8)(4) = \mathbf{64}$ cm$^{2}$/s.

The new area is a thin strip along two sides of the square, so it grows in proportion to the side length.

questions.q: Find the value of $x$ at which $f(x) = x^{2} - 4x + 5$ has its local minimum.
questions.solution:
$f'(x) = 2x - 4 = 0 \Rightarrow x = 2$.

$f''(x) = 2 > 0$, so it is a minimum. $x = \mathbf{2}$ (where $f = 1$).

For a parabola this is just the vertex, exactly halfway between the roots.

$f'(x) = -2x + 4 = 0 \Rightarrow x = 2$, and $f''(x) = -2 < 0$, so it is a maximum.

$f(2) = -4 + 8 + 5 = \mathbf{9}$.

questions.q: Use differentials to find the approximate value of $\sqrt{36.6}$, correct to three decimal places.
questions.solution:
Take $y = \sqrt{x}$ with $x = 36$ and $\Delta x = 0.6$.

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{x}} = \dfrac{1}{12}$.

$\Delta y \approx \dfrac{1}{12} \times 0.6 = 0.05$, so $\sqrt{36.6} \approx 6 + 0.05 = \mathbf{6.05}$.

(The true value is $6.0498\ldots$) The tangent line is a good stand-in for the curve as long as you do not walk far from the point of contact.

questions.q: A $5$ m ladder leans against a wall. Its foot slides away from the wall at $2$ cm/s. How fast (in cm/s) is the top sliding down when the foot is $3$ m from the wall?
questions.solution:
With $x$ along the ground and $y$ up the wall, $x^{2} + y^{2} = 25$.

Differentiate with respect to time: $2x\dfrac{dx}{dt} + 2y\dfrac{dy}{dt} = 0 \Rightarrow \dfrac{dy}{dt} = -\dfrac{x}{y}\dfrac{dx}{dt}$.

When $x = 3$, $y = 4$. So $\dfrac{dy}{dt} = -\dfrac{3}{4}(2) = -1.5$ cm/s.

The top slides **down** at $\mathbf{1.5}$ cm/s — the minus sign is the direction, the number is the speed.

questions.q: Find the intervals on which $f(x) = 2x^{3} - 3x^{2} - 36x + 7$ is increasing and on which it is decreasing.
questions.solution:
$f'(x) = 6x^{2} - 6x - 36 = 6\left(x^{2} - x - 6\right) = 6(x - 3)(x + 2)$.

The critical points are $x = -2$ and $x = 3$; test the sign of $f'$ in each stretch:

• $x < -2$: both factors negative → product positive → **increasing**.

• $-2 < x < 3$: one negative, one positive → **decreasing**.

• $x > 3$: both positive → **increasing**.

**Increasing on** $(-\infty, -2) \cup (3, \infty)$; **decreasing on** $(-2, 3)$.

The cubic climbs to a local peak at $x = -2$, dips to a local trough at $x = 3$, and climbs away.

questions.q: Find the equations of the tangent and the normal to the curve $y = x^{2} - 2x + 7$ at the point $(2, 7)$.
questions.solution:
**Check the point is on the curve:** $4 - 4 + 7 = 7$. ✓

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 2x - 2$, which at $x = 2$ is $2$ — the slope of the tangent.

**Tangent:** $y - 7 = 2(x - 2) \Rightarrow \mathbf{y = 2x + 3}$.

**Normal** is perpendicular, so its slope is $-\tfrac12$:

$y - 7 = -\tfrac12(x - 2) \Rightarrow \mathbf{x + 2y = 16}$.

Perpendicular slopes multiply to $-1$ — that single fact turns every tangent question into a normal question.

questions.topic: Maxima and minima in a real problem
questions.q: A square sheet of side $18$ cm has a small square cut from each corner, and the flaps are folded up to make an open box. Find the side of the cut square that gives the box its greatest volume.
questions.solution:
Let the cut have side $x$. The base is then $(18 - 2x)$ by $(18 - 2x)$ and the height is $x$:

$V = x\left(18 - 2x\right)^{2}$, valid for $0 < x < 9$.

$\dfrac{dV}{dx} = \left(18 - 2x\right)^{2} + x \cdot 2(18 - 2x)(-2) = (18 - 2x)\left[(18 - 2x) - 4x\right] = (18 - 2x)(18 - 6x)$.

Setting this to zero gives $x = 9$ (rejected — no box left) or $x = \mathbf{3}$ cm.

$\dfrac{d^{2}V}{dx^{2}} = 24x - 144$, which at $x = 3$ is $-72 < 0$: a maximum. ✓

The box is then $12 \times 12 \times 3$, with volume $432$ cm$^{3}$.

Cut too little and the box is shallow; cut too much and the base is tiny. The derivative finds the balance point.

questions.q: Find the absolute maximum and absolute minimum values of $f(x) = x^{3} - 3x$ on the interval $[-2, 3]$.
questions.solution:
On a closed interval the extremes can only sit at a critical point or at an endpoint, so check all of them.

$f'(x) = 3x^{2} - 3 = 0 \Rightarrow x = \pm 1$, and both lie inside $[-2, 3]$.

$f(-2) = -8 + 6 = -2$

$f(-1) = -1 + 3 = 2$

$f(1) = 1 - 3 = -2$

$f(3) = 27 - 9 = 18$

**Absolute maximum $= 18$ at $x = 3$; absolute minimum $= -2$, reached at both $x = -2$ and $x = 1$.**

The local peak at $x = -1$ is not the highest point on the interval — a local champion need not be the national one.

questions.q: The radius of a sphere is measured as $9$ cm with an error of $0.03$ cm. Find the approximate error in its calculated surface area.
questions.solution:
$S = 4\pi r^{2}$, so $\dfrac{dS}{dr} = 8\pi r$.

$\Delta S \approx 8\pi r\,\Delta r = 8\pi(9)(0.03) = \mathbf{2.16\pi}$ cm$^{2} \approx 6.79$ cm$^{2}$.

A small slip in the radius is magnified about $8\pi r$ times in the surface area — which is why measuring the radius carefully matters far more than it looks.
